claims.statement: Disconnected self-hosted runner automatically removed after more than14days; ephemeral runner after more than1day. Thresholds describe connectivity, not idle-job duration or host cleanup assurance.

Added runner/status appears in version-dependent Runners or Self-hosted runners UI; active connected application is required to accept jobs. Listing alone is not readiness, and sample connected-output include is not live evidence.

Connectivity-check example invokes config.sh with check, URL and PAT argument containing an illustrative credential-shaped literal. Do not copy the literal, acquire a token or execute; CLI token argument also requires secret-handling review.

Configuration chooses OS/architecture, references screenshot then download/install instructions. Windows service setup needs administrator shell and recommends C:\actions-runner for system-account access. Raster not visually reviewed, and no setup run.

Setup downloads/extracts app, configures destination URL with registration token expiring1hour, optionally installs Windows service or later Linux/macOS service, and starts connection. Registration token is distinct from job/scoped tokens and no credential generated.
Connected to GitHub and 2019 timestamp Listening for Jobs are illustrative terminal output; not an actual runner validation receipt or current heartbeat.
Runner group maximum10,000 self-hosted runners blocks new additions at limit according to source. Not actual group inventory or exception approval.

Default self-hosted label can be omitted by no-default-labels; recommended label array starts self-hosted and matches every label conjunctively. ARC does not support self-hosted label, so universal label prescription would break its applicability.

Runner management roles vary: personal repository owner; organization owner; organization repository owner or repo admin; GHEC enterprise owner; GHES site admin. Parent platform location statements and conditional custom-role alternatives elsewhere require reconciliation, not actual authority grants.
Organization/repository Settings navigation is a UI step, not authorization or proof of runner configuration.
Organization runner navigation opens registered organization Settings and shared runners sidebar include. Included body and observed target remain separately reviewed.
Repository runner navigation opens registered repository Settings and an organizations sidebar reusable; actual rendered suitability and target access are not proven.

Dotcom actions require outbound runner connectivity, plus GHES instance outbound when applicable; no dotcom inbound connections required. This is directional requirement, not live network observation.
Runner connection uses HTTPS443, with GHES also HTTP80 described; GHES HTTPS requires configured TLS. HTTP source support is not an adopted policy allowing insecure enterprise traffic.
Public repositories default denied group-runner use for security but settings may override; capability to override is not approval to expose runner to public fork code.

Permanent removal differs from temporary host shutdown/stopping run app, which leaves assigned runner Offline and no jobs until restarted. No stop/removal authorized or performed; future automatic disconnection removal still matters.
Unassigning label clicks a checkmarked assigned label via shared settings. No target label removed or access effect verified.

Accessible-host removal uses OS-specific command with URL/time-limited token, removing GitHub registration, app configuration and services when applicable. Without host access, Force remove deletes GitHub registration only; no claim remote host artifacts/services cleaned.
Docker container actions on self-hosted require Linux and installed Docker, not a universal Docker requirement for all actions or authorization to install.

When unable to remove registration in GitHub, source suggests deleting local .runner to re-register machine without re-download. This does not prove old remote registration removed or host sanitized; destructive source fallback is not executed or authorized.
Self-hosted security admonition wraps shared security fragment and links secure-use; actual warning content/parent rendering remain separate and no linked page implicitly reviewed.
